patch_description: Instead of returning random points, use a two-phase approach: (1) initialize with a 3-fold rotationally symmetric configuration (regular 12-gon plus center, adapted to n=13) which is known to be a strong candidate for Heilbronn-type problems, and (2) perform a deterministic projected local search — iteratively perturb points along gradient directions that increase the minimum triangle area (using the smallest triangle's vertices to guide movement), with shrinking step sizes and convex-hull normalization. The final configuration is scaled so the convex hull has exactly unit area, maximizing min_area_normalized. This exploits the symmetry heuristics and scale invariance described in the problem context, and should dramatically outperform the random baseline.
